Title: Diagnosis
Details: The reported issue describes a problem in the method JXPathContext.iteratePointers(String xpath), where multiple prefixes map to a single namespace URI, and only one element is getting returned twice while the other element in the same namespace but with a different prefix is not returned.

From the failing test snippet (testIterateDOM calls doTestIterate with DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM) and the doTestIterate method:
- It invokes assertXPathPointerIterator(createContext(model), "/a:doc/a:elem", list("/a:doc[1]/a:elem[1]", "/a:doc[1]/a:elem[2]"))
- This means it expects the iterator over the XPath "/a:doc/a:elem" to return two pointers, corresponding to two "elem" elements with prefix "a" in the document.

The bug report example shows that in the XML document:
<a:doc xmlns:a="ns">
  <a:elem />
  <b:elem xmlns:b="ns" />
</a:doc>

Here "a:elem" and "b:elem" share the same namespace URI "ns" but have different prefixes. The current implementation of iteratePointers returns the first element twice, ignoring the second element.

The assertXPathPointerIterator function collects pointers from ctx.iteratePointers(xpath), converts them to strings, and compares to the expected collection.

Because iteratePointers delegates the underlying iteration logic, it suggests that the namespace aliasing or mapping logic inside JXPathContext or its internal NamespaceContext implementation is incorrectly resolving multiple prefixes to the same namespace URI, causing the second prefixed element to be omitted. The iteratePointers method appears to treat prefixes rigidly or returns by prefix rather than by resolved namespace URI.

In conclusion, the bug is that JXPathContext.iteratePointers does not properly handle multiple prefixes mapped to the same namespace URI. This causes elements with different prefixes but same namespace URI to be incorrectly filtered out or duplicated in XPath iteration.

The test fails because it expects elements from both prefixes but only gets duplicates of one.

Suggested fix locations will need to address prefix to namespace URI resolution or the iteration logic within JXPathContext to consider all prefixes mapped to the same namespace URI uniquely.

Next, I will look at JXPathContext or internal namespace handling methods for prefix to URI aliasing or XPath evaluation methods to confirm the exact method to fix.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
